The number of subject officials in an oversight report

Source: R/ovr.R
ovrsoc.Rd

Counts the subject officials of each report, the officers whose conduct the oversight body investigated, and says which rule gave the count and on what words, so that the number can be checked against the report. Use it where a report has no roster ovrpar() can read, or to check a count coded by hand.

Usage

ovrsoc(
  x,
  tag = "SO",
  term = c("subject official", "subject officer"),
  wtag = "WO",
  head = c("Subject Officials", "Subject Officers"),
  html = NA
)

Arguments

x

The reports: pages (HTML) or texts, a character vector.

tag

The tag of a subject official in the report: one text.

term

The words for a subject official, singular: text.

wtag

The tag of a witness official: one text.

head

The headings of the roster of subject officials: text.

html

NA (the default) to read each element as HTML when it holds markup (a < followed by a letter, / or !), TRUE or FALSE to say.

Value

A data frame with one row per report: count (whole number, NA when unresolved), rule (1 to 6, as above) and reason (the rule and the words it read).

Details

The rules run in order and the first that applies gives the count:

  1. the roster under a heading of head: the highest numbered tag there ("SO #2");

  2. the highest numbered tag in the whole report, trusted only when the tag numbered 1 is there too;

  3. a number before a plural of term ("two subject officials", "3 subject officers");

  4. a mention of term in the singular, not after "no" or "not a": 1;

  5. a statement that there was none ("no subject official"), or numbered witness tags (wtag) with no subject tag at all: 0, a real answer;

  6. otherwise unresolved: NA.

Tags and headings are matched as written; term in any case. The defaults are the words of Canadian oversight bodies; give a body's own (tag = "AI", term = "agent impliqué" for a French report).

Examples

ovrsoc(c("Subject Officials\nSO #1 Interviewed\nSO #2 Declined",
         "Two subject officials were designated.",
         "Witness Officials\nWO #1\nWO #2",
         "No officers are named here."))
#>   count rule                                      reason
#> 1     2    1 the roster under the heading: highest SO #2
#> 2     2    3           a plural: 'Two subject officials'
#> 3     0    5               witness officials only: WO #2
#> 4    NA    6                                  unresolved
